stotra.description: The Purusha Suktam gives a description of the spiritual unity of the universe.

shlokas.full_sanskrit:
स॒हस्र॑शीर्​षा॒ पुरु॑षः । स॒ह॒स्रा॒क्ष-स्स॒हस्र॑पात् ।
स भूमिं॑-विँ॒श्वतो॑ वृ॒त्वा । अत्य॑तिष्ठद्दशाङ्गु॒लम् ॥
shlokas.sandhi_split_sanskrit: सहस्रशीर्षा | पुरुषः | सहस्राक्षः | सहस्रपात् | स | भूमिं | विश्वतः | वृत्वा | अत्यतिष्ठत् | दशाङुलम्
shlokas.iast_transliteration: sahasraśīrṣā puruṣaḥ । sahasrākṣa-ssahasrapāt । sa bhūmiṃ viśvatō vṛtvā । atyatiṣṭhaddaśāṅgulam ॥
shlokas.meaning_english: The purusha (universal being) has thousand heads, thousand eyes and thousand feet. Thousand signifies innumerable which points to the omnipresence of the universal being. He envelops the world from all sides i.e. he pervades each part of the creation, and extends beyond in the ten directions represented by ten fingers.

shlokas.full_sanskrit:
पुरु॑ष ए॒वेदग्ं सर्वम्᳚ । यद्भू॒तं-यँच्च॒ भव्यम्᳚ ।
उ॒तामृ॑त॒त्व स्येशा॑नः । यदन्ने॑नाति॒रोह॑ति ॥
shlokas.sandhi_split_sanskrit: पुरुष | एव | इदं | सर्वं | यत् | भूतं | यत् | च | भव्यम् | उत | अमृतत्वस्य | ईशानः | यत् | अन्नेन | अतिरोहति
shlokas.iast_transliteration: puruṣa ēvēdagṃ sarvam । yadbhūtaṃ yachcha bhavyam । utāmṛtatva syēśānaḥ । yadannēnātirōhati ॥
shlokas.meaning_english: The purusha is indeed all this (creation) in essence; that which existed in the past, and that which will exist in the future, everything i.e the whole creation is woven by the immortal essence of the great lord (purusha); by becoming food of which (i.e. by getting consumed in whose immortal essence through surrender) one transcends the gross world and becomes immortal.

shlokas.full_sanskrit:
ए॒तावा॑नस्य महि॒मा । अतो॒ ज्यायाग्॑श्च॒ पूरु॑षः ।
पादो᳚-ऽस्य॒ विश्वा॑ भू॒तानि॑ । त्रि॒पाद॑स्या॒मृत॑-न्दि॒वि ॥
shlokas.sandhi_split_sanskrit: एतावान् | अस्य | महिमा | अतः | ज्यायान् | च | पूरुषः | पादः | अस्य | विश्वा | भूतानि | त्रिपादस्य | अमृतं | दिवि
shlokas.iast_transliteration: ētāvānasya mahimā । atō jyāyāgścha pūruṣaḥ । pādō-'sya viśvā bhūtāni । tripādasyāmṛta-ndivi ॥
shlokas.meaning_english: The purusha is greater than all the greatness which can be expressed by words. His one part has become all these (visible) worlds, and his three parts rest in the immortal world of the transcendence.

shlokas.full_sanskrit:
त्रि॒पादू॒र्ध्व उदै॒त्पुरु॑षः । पादो᳚-ऽस्ये॒हा-ऽऽभ॑वा॒त्पुनः॑ ।
ततो॒ विष्व॒ङ्​व्य॑क्रामत् । सा॒श॒ना॒न॒श॒ने अ॒भि ॥
shlokas.sandhi_split_sanskrit: त्रिपाद् | ऊर्ध्व | उदैत् | पूरुषः | पादः | अस्य | इह | अभवत् | पुनः | ततः | विष्वङ् | व्यक्रामत् | साशन | अनशने | अभि
shlokas.iast_transliteration: tripādūrdhva udaitpuruṣaḥ । pādō-'syēhā-''bhavātpunaḥ । tatō viṣvaṅvyakrāmat । sāśanānaśanē abhi ॥
shlokas.meaning_english: The three parts of the purusha is high above (in transcendental realm), and his one part becomes the creation again and again. There, in the creation, he pervades all the living ( who eats ) and the non-living ( who does not eat ) beings.

shlokas.full_sanskrit:
तस्मा᳚द्वि॒राड॑जायत । वि॒राजो॒ अधि॒ पूरु॑षः ।
स जा॒तो अत्य॑रिच्यत । प॒श्चाद्भूमि॒मथो॑ पु॒रः ॥
shlokas.sandhi_split_sanskrit: तस्मात् | विराट् | अजायत | विराजः | अधि | पूरुषः | सः | जातः | अत्यरिच्यत | पश्चात् | भूमिम् | अथ | पुरः
shlokas.iast_transliteration: tasmādvirāḍajāyata । virājō adhi pūruṣaḥ । sa jātō atyarichyata । paśchādbhūmimathō puraḥ ॥
shlokas.meaning_english: From purusha was born the virat; (the virat came into being) from the presence of the shining purusha (who remained as the background or substratum of virat); he (i.e. the virat) created the earth, by manifesting her from his own being as substratum.

shlokas.full_sanskrit:
यत्पुरु॑षेण ह॒विषा᳚ । दे॒वा य॒ज्ञमत॑न्वत ।
व॒स॒न्तो अ॑स्यासी॒दाज्यम्᳚ । ग्री॒ष्म इ॒ध्मश्श॒रध्ध॒विः ॥
shlokas.sandhi_split_sanskrit: यत् | पुरुषेण | हविषा | देवाः | यज्ञम् | अतन्वत | वसन्तः | अस्य | आसीत् | आज्यम् | ग्रीष्मः | इध्मः | शरद् | धविः
shlokas.iast_transliteration: yatpuruṣēṇa haviṣā । dēvā yajñamatanvata । vasantō asyāsīdājyam । grīṣma idhmaśśaradhdhaviḥ ॥
shlokas.meaning_english: With the purusha as the (sacrificial) fire, the deva (the shining one, referring to virat) continued the yagna (sacrifice of creation), spring was (created as) the clarified butter (of that yagna), summer was (created as) the fuel (of that yagna), and autumn was (created as) the havis (sacrificial offering of that yagna).

shlokas.full_sanskrit:
स॒प्तास्या॑सन्परि॒धयः॑ । त्रि-स्स॒प्त स॒मिधः॑ कृ॒ताः ।
दे॒वा यद्य॒ज्ञ-न्त॑न्वा॒नाः । अब॑ध्न॒न्-पुरु॑ष-म्प॒शुम् ॥
shlokas.sandhi_split_sanskrit: सप्त | अस्य | आसन | परिधयः | त्रिः | सप्त | समिधः | कृताः | देवाः | यत् | यज्ञं | तन्वानाः | अबध्नन् | पुरुषं | पशुम्
shlokas.iast_transliteration: saptāsyāsanparidhayaḥ । tri-ssapta samidhaḥ kṛtāḥ । dēvā yadyajña-ntanvānāḥ । abadhnan-puruṣa-mpaśum ॥
shlokas.meaning_english: By making seven enclosures with three times seven sacrificial firewood, the deva (the shining one referring to virat) in that yagna (sacrifice of creation), bound the infinite expanse of the purusha as (apparently) finite living beings (pashu).

shlokas.full_sanskrit:
तं-यँ॒ज्ञ-म्ब॒र्॒हिषि॒ प्रौक्षन्॑ । पुरु॑ष-ञ्जा॒तम॑ग्र॒तः ।
तेन॑ दे॒वा अय॑जन्त । सा॒ध्या ऋष॑यश्च॒ ये ॥
shlokas.sandhi_split_sanskrit: तं | यज्ञं | बर्हिषि | प्रौक्षन् | पुरुषं | जातम् | अग्रतः | तेन | देवाः | अयजन्त | साध्याः | ऋषयः | च | ये
shlokas.iast_transliteration: taṃ yajña-mbarhiṣi praukṣan । puruṣa-ñjātamagrataḥ । tēna dēvā ayajanta । sādhyā ṛṣayaścha yē ॥
shlokas.meaning_english: The first divine men were created as the holy water sprinkled with the kusa grass in that yagna (sacrifice of creation). the first divine men were the sadhya devas and the rishis, who were created by him, the deva (the shining one, referring to virat), who performed the yagna. These rishis were not human but divine rishis like saptarshis created directly by virat.

shlokas.full_sanskrit:
तस्मा᳚द्य॒ज्ञाथ्स॑र्व॒हुतः॑ । सम्भृ॑त-म्पृषदा॒ज्यम् ।
प॒शूग्-स्ताग्-श्च॑क्रे वाय॒व्यान्॑ । आ॒र॒ण्यान्-ग्रा॒म्याश्च॒ ये ॥
shlokas.sandhi_split_sanskrit: तस्मात् | यज्ञात् | सर्वहुतः | सम्भृतं | पृषदाज्यम् | पशून् | ताँश्च | चक्रे | वायव्यान् | आरण्यान् | ग्राम्याः | च | ये
shlokas.iast_transliteration: tasmādyajñāthsarvahutaḥ । sambhṛta-mpṛṣadājyam । paśūg-stāg-śchakrē vāyavyān । āraṇyān-grāmyāścha yē ॥
shlokas.meaning_english: From the complete offering of his (i.e. virat's) yagna (sacrifice of creation) was obtained ghee mixed with coagulated milk, which (i.e. the ghee and milk) are (the created) animals, both of air (birds) and of forests (wild animals) and villages (domestic animals).

shlokas.full_sanskrit:
तस्मा᳚द्य॒ज्ञाथ्स॑र्व॒हुतः॑ । ऋच॒-स्सामा॑नि जज्ञिरे ।
छन्दाग्ं॑सि जज्ञिरे॒ तस्मा᳚त् । यजु॒स्तस्मा॑दजायत ॥
shlokas.sandhi_split_sanskrit: तस्मात् | यज्ञात् | सर्वहुत | ऋचः | सामानि | जज्ञिरे | छन्दांसि | जज्ञिरे | तस्मात् | यजुः | तस्मात् | अजायत
shlokas.iast_transliteration: tasmādyajñāthsarvahutaḥ । ṛcha-ssāmāni jajñirē । Chandāgṃsi jajñirē tasmāt । yajustasmādajāyata ॥
shlokas.meaning_english: From the complete offering of his (i.e. virat's) yagna (sacrifice of creation) was born the rig veda and sama veda, the chandas (vedic meters) were born from him, and the yajur veda was born from him.

shlokas.full_sanskrit:
तस्मा॒दश्वा॑ अजायन्त । ये के चो॑भ॒याद॑तः ।
गावो॑ ह जज्ञिरे॒ तस्मा᳚त् । तस्मा᳚ज्जा॒ता अ॑जा॒वयः॑ ॥
shlokas.sandhi_split_sanskrit: तस्मात् | अश्वाः | अजायन्त | ये | के | च | उभयादतः | गावः | ह | जज्ञिरे | तस्मात् | तस्मात् | जाताः | अजावयः
shlokas.iast_transliteration: tasmādaśvā ajāyanta । yē kē chōbhayādataḥ । gāvō ha jajñirē tasmāt । tasmājjātā ajāvayaḥ ॥
shlokas.meaning_english: From him (i.e. virat) was born the horses, and all those animals who has teeth in both jaws, from him (i.e. virat) was born the cows, and from him was born all types of goats.

shlokas.full_sanskrit:
यत्पुरु॑षं॒-व्यँ॑दधुः । क॒ति॒था व्य॑कल्पयन्न् ।
मुख॒-ङ्किम॑स्य॒ कौ बा॒हू । कावू॒रू पादा॑वुच्येते ॥
shlokas.sandhi_split_sanskrit: यत् | पुरुषम् | व्यदधुः | कतिधा | विकल्पयन् | मुखम् | किम् | अस्य | कौ | बाहू | का | ऊरू | पादाः | उच्येते
shlokas.iast_transliteration: yatpuruṣaṃ vyadadhuḥ । katithā vyakalpayann । mukha-ṅkimasya kau bāhū । kāvūrū pādāvuchyētē ॥
shlokas.meaning_english: What did the purusha (i.e. virat) hold within him? How many parts were assigned in his huge form? What was his mouth? What was his arms? What was his thighs? And what was his feet?

shlokas.full_sanskrit:
ब्रा॒ह्म॒णो᳚-ऽस्य॒ मुख॑मासीत् । बा॒हू रा॑ज॒न्यः॑ कृ॒तः ।
ऊ॒रू तद॑स्य॒ यद्वैश्यः॑ । प॒द्भ्याग्ं शू॒द्रो अ॑जायत ॥
shlokas.sandhi_split_sanskrit: ब्राह्मणः | अस्य | मुखम् | आसीत् | बाहू | राजन्यः | कृतः | ऊरू | तत् | अस्य | यत् | वैश्यः | पद्भ्याम् | शूद्रः | अजायत
shlokas.iast_transliteration: brāhmaṇō-'sya mukhamāsīt । bāhū rājanyaḥ kṛtaḥ । ūrū tadasya yadvaiśyaḥ । padbhyāgṃ śūdrō ajāyata ॥
shlokas.meaning_english: The Brahmanas were his mouth, the kshatriyas became his arms, the vaishyas were his thighs, and the shudras were assigned to his feet.

shlokas.full_sanskrit:
च॒न्द्रमा॒ मन॑सो जा॒तः । चक्षो॒-स्सूर्यो॑ अजायत ।
मुखा॒दिन्द्र॑श्चा॒ग्निश्च॑ । प्रा॒णाद्वा॒युर॑जायत ॥
shlokas.sandhi_split_sanskrit: चन्द्रमा | मनसः | जातः | चक्षोः | सूर्यः | अजायत | मुखात् | इन्द्रः | च | अग्निः | च | प्राणात् | वायुः | अजायत
shlokas.iast_transliteration: chandramā manasō jātaḥ । chakṣō-ssūryō ajāyata । mukhādindraśchāgniścha । prāṇādvāyurajāyata ॥
shlokas.meaning_english: The moon was born from his mind and the sun was born from his eyes, Indra and agni (fire) were born from his mouth, and vayu (wind) was born from his breath.

shlokas.full_sanskrit:
नाभ्या॑ आसीद॒न्तरि॑क्षम् । शी॒र्​ष्णो द्यौ-स्सम॑वर्तत ।
प॒द्भ्या-म्भूमि॒र्दिश॒-श्श्रोत्रा᳚त् । तथा॑ लो॒काग्ं अ॑कल्पयन्न् ॥
shlokas.sandhi_split_sanskrit: नाभ्या | आसीत् | अन्तरिक्षं | शीर्ष्णः | द्यौः | समवर्तत | पद्भ्याम् | भूमिः | दिशः | श्रोत्रात् | तथा | लोकान् | अकल्पयन्
shlokas.iast_transliteration: nābhyā āsīdantarikṣam । śīrṣṇō dyau-ssamavartata । padbhyā-mbhūmirdiśa-śśrōtrāt । tathā lōkāgṃ akalpayann ॥
shlokas.meaning_english: His navel became the antariksha (the intermediate space between heaven and earth), his head sustained the heaven, from his feet the earth (was sustained), and from his ears the directions (were sustained); in this manner all the worlds were regulated by him.

shlokas.full_sanskrit:
वेदा॒हमे॒त-म्पुरु॑ष-म्म॒हान्तम्᳚ । आ॒दि॒त्यव॑र्ण॒-न्तम॑स॒स्तु पा॒रे ।
सर्वा॑णि रू॒पाणि॑ वि॒चित्य॒ धीरः॑ । नामा॑नि कृ॒त्वा-ऽभि॒वद॒न्॒, यदा-ऽऽस्ते᳚ ॥
shlokas.sandhi_split_sanskrit: वेद-अहम् | एतम्-पुरुषम्-महान्तम् | आदित्य-वर्णम् | तमसः तु पारे | सर्वाणि रूपाणि | विचित्य | धीरः | नामानि कृत्वा | अभिवदन् | यदा आस्ते
shlokas.iast_transliteration: vēdāhamēta-mpuruṣa-mmahāntam । ādityavarṇa-ntamasastu pārē । sarvāṇi rūpāṇi vichitya dhīraḥ । nāmāni kṛtvā-'bhivadan, yadā-''stē ॥
shlokas.meaning_english: I know this great Purusha, radiant as the sun, beyond all darkness. The wise one, having discerned all forms and having created their names, speaks of them — and thus He abides eternally.
